title: Critical Sets in Latin Squares and Associated Structures
summary: A critical set in a Latin square of order $n$ is a set of entries in an $n\times n$ array which can be embedded in precisely one Latin square of order $n$, with the property that if any entry of the critical set is deleted, the remaining set can be embedded in more than one Latin square of order $n$. The cardinality of the largest critical set in any Latin square of order $n$ is denoted by $lcs(n)$. In 1978 Curran and van Rees proved that $lcs(n)\leq n^2-n$.
